analysis: This batch contains only small changes, and none shows a concrete regression. (1) ProviderLoop.swift head 444-445 adds `loadWeightHasher`, which defaults to WeightHasher.computeHash and serves as the full weight read behind captureWeightHash. The default is identical to the existing modelSwitchWeightHasher, and production behavior depends on how captureWeightHash uses it; that code is not supplied. (2) ProviderLoop.swift head 684-688 adds `verifiedWeightHashesFile: URL?` (VerifiedWeightHashStore). The comment says verified managed-load hashes are recorded 'for the next start's registration' and stay nil until run() serves with host services. This is new on-disk state under TB-003. If the next registration advertises a persisted hash without re-hashing the current weights, an operator (ADV-001) could swap weights after a verified load and keep advertising the old weightHash. That would weaken the T-012/T-027 weight-substitution checks and the T-041 SSD cache weightHash binding. The store implementation, file location and permissions, and the registration and preload consumers are not in this batch. Integration must verify that a persisted hash is only a hint and that fresh cryptographic hashing (requireFreshCryptographicHash, finalizeReusableSSDLoad) runs before advertising or SSD-cache binding. (3) ProviderLoop+Testing.swift head 143-152 adds test-only setters for these fields. They are not under #if DEBUG, like most existing seams, and are internal and reachable only via @testable import; no new production surface was identified. (4) ProviderLoop+Trust.swift head 129 calls GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice.report(failureMessage:modelID:) on model-load failures. Its sink (log, stdout or file) is not supplied. Load-error messages are operator diagnostics and are not expected to contain A-001 consumer plaintext; this should be confirmed in integration. Base 1-543 of ProviderLoop.swift and the trust-status persistence logic are otherwise unchanged.
